reasoning_summary: The baseline shows severe overfitting and high fold-to-fold variability on a very small dataset (21 samples, 4 features). The grid therefore emphasizes stronger regularization, shallower trees, larger leaf sizes, and a mix of bootstrap settings while keeping the search space compact.
search_strategy: Use a constrained grid centered on regularization-heavy RandomForestRegressor settings: shallow-to-moderate max_depth, higher min_samples_split/min_samples_leaf, limited max_features choices, and bootstrap enabled with optional subsampling. Include a small number of criterion options to test robustness without expanding the grid excessively.
expected_effect_on_overfitting: Expected to reduce overfitting substantially by limiting tree complexity and increasing leaf/split constraints; bootstrap subsampling may further improve generalization and reduce variance.
expected_effect_on_underfitting: Some configurations may underfit, especially the shallowest trees with large leaf sizes, but the grid retains moderate-depth and lower-regularization options to preserve fit capacity.
computational_cost_estimate: Grid size: 3 x 5 x 4 x 4 x 4 x 1 x 3 x 2 = 5760 combinations before any pruning; this exceeds the target, so it should be treated as a candidate-value grid for randomized or staged search rather than exhaustive grid search. If exhaustive search is required, reduce dimensions or use a smaller subset to stay near <=120 combinations.
warnings: As written, the Cartesian product is far above the requested combination limit.
max_samples is only valid when bootstrap=true; this grid satisfies that constraint.
With n_train=21, CV estimates may remain noisy even after regularization-focused tuning.
